text:
ops-bot: INCIDENT alert — capacity-tier-routing anomaly detected for tenant=acme-corp, ratio of hosted->dedicated spillover abnormal (>12% in last 5m) :rotating_light:
Alex Chen: seeing 5xx spikes from acme-corp dashboards, started ~10:12UTC. latency up and errors on hosted frontends.
Alex Chen: can someone confirm whether routing-policy rollout 2026-03-15/auto-tiering was applied to that tenant?
Maria Gomez: checking policy history now — I see a canary update at 10:04 that touched 'smart-tier:prefer-dedicated' thresholds. looks like a bad threshold change.
Jordan (oncall): paging SREs, I'm oncall and moving to incident channel. @Raj can you look at pool assignments?
Raj Patel: pulling pool bindings — `redwood routing list-assignments --tenant acme-corp` shows active binding to dedicated-pool-3 which is unexpected; binding TTL set to 0 (sticky).
Tessa Li: Sticky TTL 0 was from the policy rollout, it forces dedicated bind until manually cleared. that's probably the regresssion.
Alex Chen: customer impact — acme-corp on hosted plans, now their traffic hits dedicated where qos and isolation differ -> errors and token billing mismatch. we should treat this P1 for customer impact.
Emily Park: I'll open a support ticket and notify account team. what mitigations can we do immediately?
Raj Patel: quick mitigation: flip circuit-breaker for tenant at routing layer -> `redwood routing set-circuit --tenant acme-corp --mode=hosted-only --expires=30m` to force traffic back to hosted.
Jordan (oncall): executing now. `> redwood routing set-circuit --tenant acme-corp --mode=hosted-only --expires=30m`
ops-bot: action logged by Jordan (oncall) — circuit applied, routing delta observed.
Alex Chen: good, error rate dropped within 60s. keep circuit for 30m while we rollback policy.
Maria Gomez: policy rollout v2026-03-15/auto-tiering will be rolled back to v2026-03-08 now. running `redwood policy rollback --name auto-tiering --to=2026-03-08 --apply`
Tessa Li: rollback in progress. also removing the sticky TTL patch from canary.
ops-bot: rollback completed at 10:26UTC.
Raj Patel: verifying assignments — `redwood routing list-assignments --tenant acme-corp` now shows hosted assignment, no TTL. confirming no cross-tenant breach.
Alex Chen: quick security check — any logs suggesting requests served under wrong tenant isolation or data leakage?
Tessa Li: initial audit shows 0 suspicious cross-tenant KV accesses. dedicated pool had requests from acme-corp only. main risk was billing/perf, not data exfil.
Emily Park: informing acme-corp support: "We experienced a routing policy regression that temporarily routed your traffic to a dedicated pool. We've reverted the policy and forced routing back; there is no evidence of data exposure. Apologies, we'll follow up with root cause and compensation."
Jordan (oncall): will keep monitoring for 1 hour after circuit expiry and then remove circuit if stable. I'm handing off to Tessa for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
Tessa Li: taking ownership for postmortem and fix. planned action items: 1) add preflight check for sticky TTL changes, 2) add automated canary rollback on dedicated-bind-rate > 5% of tenant traffic, 3) run an audit job to re-check pool bindings for tenants with recent policy changes.
Alex Chen: also add a routing policy unit test that simulates small-traffic tenants to catch this.
ops-bot: incident status -> mitigated, P1 -> postmortem assigned to Tessa Li.
Maria Gomez: tagging config PR 4823 as revert candidate; will follow up with infra deploy safe window.
Emily Park: sent initial customer note and created support case SC-20260315-775.
Jordan (oncall): handoff to Tessa at 10:40UTC. I'll unpage unless something spikes.
Tessa Li: got it — will publish timeline and RCA by EOD tomorrow. :memo:
Alex Chen: thanks everyone.
